rendered:
The premise needs a correction: the Cyrene separation itself was not run at room temperature. The key separation steps were run hot, at 100 °C[1], because PVDF is barely soluble in Cyrene at lower temperatures and precipitates out if the temperature drops. PVDF would precipitate out if the temperature was low[2]. Hot filtration and hot centrifugation were therefore used to separate the foils and cathode powder from the solution without PVDF re-precipitating.

Room temperature was used for a recovery step and as a control. For recovery, the hot supernatant was cooled to room temperature so that phase separation would precipitate the PVDF together with residual carbon black. By cooling down the hot supernatant to room temperature[3], and the PVDF/CB composite was filtered off along with the recycled Cyrene. As a control, a room-temperature filtration was run to show the effect of cooling. FTIR found the PVDF band in the cathode powder filtered at room temperature, indicating PVDF had re-precipitated onto the particles, while the powder filtered hot did not show it.
